assessment: This work has important implications on how we view and understand social and individual learning with respect to dopamine processing in the human brain. This study, supported by a well-controlled experimental design, clear hypothesis testing, and rigorous model-based analyses, revealed that the dopamine system is involved in learning from a primary source as opposed to a secondary source, irrespective of social or non-social individual learning. This work encourages new investigations into testing when and how different neuromodulator systems may converge or diverge in guiding social versus non-social learning.
